fca2014.title: Final Notice to Royal Bank of Scotland Plc, National Westminster Bank Plc and Ulster Bank Ltd (reference numbers 121882, 121878 and 122315)
fca2014.author: Financial Conduct Authority
fca2014.quote: As a result of backing out the software upgrade, a significant number of jobs failed to appear in the batch queues and the unprocessed batch jobs began to multiply.
supports: 4.5: 'Batch schedulers place the jobs into queues and ensure that each job is processed in the correct sequence. That day's batch processing is complete when all balances are final.'

4.6: 'On Sunday 17 June 2012 a team from Technology Services upgraded the batch scheduler software that processed updates to customers' accounts at NatWest and Ulster Bank because this software could no longer be sufficiently supported. They upgraded the batch scheduler software from Version 1 to Version 2A. Version 2A contained a modification known as a "patch".'

4.7: 'On the evening of Monday 18 June 2012, the Technology Services team executed the first full batch run (set of updates) for the NatWest and Ulster Bank batch scheduler since the software update. During the evening the team noticed a number of anomalies.'

4.8: 'On Tuesday 19 June 2012, Technology Services backed out the software upgrade. ... Technology Services had only tested the consequences of backing out Version 2 to Version 1. They had not tested the consequences of backing out Version 2A to Version 1. This was the underlying cause of the IT Incident.'
4.10: 'To resolve the problem, technical support staff focused on manually re-loading jobs into the batch queues.'

4.11: 'By 21 June 2012, batch processing for Ulster Bank was more than one day behind. This meant that the next day's batch processing started before the current day's batch processing was complete. The simultaneous processing of Ulster Bank's batches interfered with each other because there were multiple days' files in the processing system and multiple days' jobs in the queues. This caused additional recovery problems and further backlogs.'
4.13: 'The Ulster Bank batch scheduler did not return to full functionality until 10 July 2012.'

2.3: 'Customers would later find that the Banks had applied incorrect credit and debit interest to their accounts, duplicated entries on their statements and failed to accurately record transactions on their accounts. Customers also learned that the Banks had not processed their standing orders on time.'
2.8: 'The IT Incident affected at least 6.5 million customers in the UK (92% of whom were UK retail customers). This was 10% of the population.'
1.1: 'a financial penalty of GBP 42,000,000 for breaches of Principle 3 between 1 August 2010 and 10 July 2012'
1.2: 'Were it not for this discount, the Authority would have imposed a financial penalty of GBP 60,000,000 on the Banks.'
2.16: 'The Banks paid approximately GBP 70.3 million in redress to UK customers. In addition, they paid redress of GBP 460,000 to individuals and firms who were not their customers.'
2.15: 'Customers (including those of Ulster Bank ROI) filed almost 70,000 complaints and non-customers filed 1,200 complaints.'

4.41: 'Group Internal Audit finalised an audit of the mainframe batch processes in August 2010. This included the back out procedures for changes to the relevant batch scheduler software. Group Internal Audit's terms of reference and its scoping documents for that project correctly identified the potential for a batch processing failure.'
4.58: Group Board minutes, July 2012 - 'with hindsight, batch processing was taken for granted and attention was focussed on technology that had failed or future developments'.
2.2: 'Customers ... were unable to drawdown loans, transfer payments to external creditors including credit card companies and mortgage providers or transfer monies using SWIFT payment methods.'

2.4: 'The problems affected not only the Banks' customers in the UK. They also affected customers who were abroad. The Banks declined their credit card purchases leaving customers unable to pay bills and make purchases. Some customers found themselves without access to cash in foreign countries.'
2.6: 'Other commercial customers were unable to finalise their audited accounts and meet payroll commitments.'
2.9: 'Technology Services (the centralised Group IT function which provides IT services to the Banks)'
2.13: 'The Banks' breaches took place between 1 August 2010 (the date of a Group Internal Audit on mainframe batch processes, which identified the risk of a batch scheduler failure) and 10 July 2012'
Annex 1.3: 'In April 2013, the FCA and PRA agreed to undertake a joint investigation into the IT Incident.'

pra2014.title: Final Notice to Royal Bank of Scotland Plc, National Westminster Bank Plc and Ulster Bank Ltd (Prudential Regulation Authority)
pra2014.author: Prudential Regulation Authority, Bank of England
pra2014.quote: For the reasons set out in this Notice, the PRA imposes on the Royal Bank of Scotland Plc, National Westminster Bank Plc and Ulster Bank Ltd (insofar as it applies to its operations in Northern Ireland) (together the "Banks"), a financial penalty of £14,000,000.
supports: 1.2: 'The Banks agreed to settle at an early stage of the PRA's investigation and therefore qualified for a 30% (stage 1) discount under the PRA's Settlement Policy. Were it not for this discount, the PRA would have imposed a financial penalty of GBP 20,000,000 on the Banks.'
2.1: 'The PRA adopts and relies upon the "Facts and Matters" section as set out in the FCA Final Notice in reaching its decision.'

Annex B 1.6: 'As a result of backing out the version of the batch scheduler software, a significant number of jobs failed to appear in the batch queues and increasing numbers of unprocessed batch jobs began to multiply.'

fcapr2014.title: FCA fines RBS, NatWest and Ulster Bank Ltd £42 million for IT failures (press release)
fcapr2014.author: Financial Conduct Authority
fcapr2014.quote: Modern banking depends on effective, reliable and resilient IT systems. The Banks' failures meant millions of customers were unable to carry out the banking transactions which keep businesses and people's everyday lives moving.
supports: First published: 20/11/2014.
Attribution: 'Tracey McDermott, director of enforcement and financial crime at the FCA said:'
'Today's fine is the first time the FCA and the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) have taken joint enforcement action. The PRA has fined the Banks £14 million.'

'Shortly after the IT incident, the FCA wrote to the chairmen of major retail banks in 2012 to ask them to identify the steps they had considered at board level to assess and mitigate their exposure to IT risks.'
'The RBS Group spends over £1 billion annually to maintain IT infrastructure.'

unverified: That the batch scheduler product was CA Technologies' CA-7. Widely reported in trade press, but neither the FCA nor the PRA Final Notice names the vendor or product - both say only 'batch scheduler software', 'Version 1' and 'Version 2A'. Not used in the prose.

The frequently cited ~£175M total remediation/incident cost. The FCA Final Notice records £70.3 million redress to UK customers plus £460,000 to non-customers, and gives no total remediation figure. Only the Final Notice figures are used.
Stephen Hester's waiver of his 2012 bonus after the incident. Named in neither Final Notice; not used, and no card names him.
The number of jobs in a single NatWest/Ulster Bank nightly batch run.
The PRA Final Notice PDF returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool and was retrieved directly with curl; text extracted from the downloaded PDF.

Which regulator's notice carries which figure: the FCA Final Notice never states the PRA's £14,000,000 penalty. That figure is cited only to pra2014 (PRA Final Notice 1.1) in the prose and to fcapr2014 (press release) on the person card; it was removed from the two cards whose cite key is fca2014.
